decision: Promising small-sample relevance gains, insufficient evidence for production replacement
source: BEIR SciFact published scientific-claim evidence retrieval qrels; Wadden et al.2020 and Thakur et al.2021
design: Eight frozen seeded English test queries and eight unreviewed AI Korean translations; identical English BM25 top10 candidate pools from5183 abstracts, no gold injection, current standard HybridRanker versus unchanged JEV Score rubric.

validation_fix.finding: Original probability validation incorrectly rejected some independently hundredth-rounded API values, including probabilities summing to0.99.
validation_fix.change: Bounded four-bin rounding allowances:0.02 probability sum and0.035 expected-score discrepancy plus floating epsilon; no normalization or altered raw scores.

limitations: English gain interval includes zero and is based on only8 independent claims; one query improves and one regresses. No statistically established general superiority.
Korean uses unreviewed translations and borrowed English labels, not independent human Korean judgments. Bootstrap intervals with few non-tied queries must not be treated as deployment proof.
Unlisted qrel candidates are assigned zero only by benchmark convention, not verified irrelevant. One sampled query has no gold in the candidate pool.
Three recovered scores were requested after the numerical-validation correction; other scores remain frozen, so the final comparison is a mixed-time recovery, not a complete fresh rerun.
Scientific-claim evidence retrieval is narrower than general scholarly search. This does not test all author/year/exclusion filters or establish general Korean search quality.
Prior latency regression and timeouts remain relevant; this quality result does not remove those operational costs.
recommendation: Keep existing production ranking. Treat JEV as an optional evaluation candidate; require larger independently reviewed Korean and domain-specific holdout evidence plus latency improvement before deployment.
